Favored Enemy

Weapon Mastery
Light Crossbow (Slow — target speed −10 ft) · Warhammer (Push — push 10 ft)




🎭 Illusionist Subclass Features (Wizard 3)






Improved Illusions — applies to all Illusion school spells Tiberius casts:

No verbal components — all Illusion spells can be cast without the verbal (V) component. Silence, stealth, restraint — no problem.
Extended range — if an Illusion spell has a range of 10 ft or more, the range increases by 60 ft.

Minor Illusion: 30 → 90 ft · Silent Image: 60 → 120 ft (Touch spells unchanged)

Minor Illusion (always known): Can create a sound and an image simultaneously with a single casting. Can be cast as a Bonus Action instead of an Action.






⚔️ War Caster (Wizard 4 feat)







Concentration: Advantage on CON saves to maintain concentration when taking damage — huge for Invisibility, Magic Weapon, Silent Image, etc.
Hands full: Can perform somatic spell components even with weapons or a shield in both hands
Opportunity spell: When a hostile creature’s movement triggers an opportunity attack, you can cast a 1-action spell targeting that creature instead of the normal attack

title: Spellbook
text:
⭐ = Prepared / Always Prepared · C = Concentration · R = Ritual · Mage Armor struck through — medium armor is better




Cantrips



  
  
    
      Fire Bolt
      Evocation Cantrip · Wizard
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range120 ft
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      You hurl a mote of fire at a creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 fire damage. A flammable object hit by this spell ignites if it isn't being worn or carried.
    
    Cantrip Upgrade: 2d10 at level 5 · 3d10 at level 11 · 4d10 at level 17
    Wizard spellbook · Attack: +7
  

  
  
    
      Poison Spray
      Necromancy Cantrip · Wizard
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range10 ft
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      You extend your hand toward a creature you can see within range and project a puff of noxious gas. The creature must succeed on a CON saving throw (DC 15) or take 1d12 poison damage.
    
    Cantrip Upgrade: 2d12 at level 5 · 3d12 at level 11 · 4d12 at level 17
    Wizard spellbook
  

  
  
    
      True Strike (2024)
      Evocation Cantrip · Wizard
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      RangeSelf (melee/ranged)
      ComponentsS (no V!)
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      Guided by a flash of magical insight, you make one attack with a weapon or unarmed strike — or one melee or ranged spell attack. You can use your spellcasting ability (INT) instead of STR or DEX for the attack and damage rolls. On a hit, the target takes 1d6 + INT modifier radiant damage.
      Unlike the 2014 version, this is an attack cantrip — no more forfeiting your action to gain advantage.
    
    Cantrip Upgrade: 2d6 at level 5 · 3d6 at level 11 · 4d6 at level 17
    Wizard spellbook · Attack: +7 (INT)
  

  
  
    
      Guidance
      Divination Cantrip · Cleric (Acolyte background)
    
    C
    
      Casting TimeAction
      RangeTouch
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationConcentration, 1 min
    
    
      You touch one willing creature. Once before the spell ends, the target can roll a d4 and add the number rolled to one ability check of its choice. The creature can roll the die before or after making the ability check. The spell then ends.
    
    Acolyte background (Cleric cantrip)
  

  
  
    
      Thaumaturgy
      Transmutation Cantrip · Cleric (Acolyte background)
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range30 ft
      ComponentsV
      DurationUp to 1 minute
    
    
      You manifest a minor wonder, a sign of supernatural power. Choose one of the following effects:
      • Your voice booms up to 3× louder for 1 minute.
      • You cause flames to flicker, brighten, dim, or change colour for 1 minute.
      • You cause harmless tremors in the ground for 1 minute.
      • You create an instantaneous sound that originates from a point you choose within range.
      • You instantaneously cause an unlocked door or window to fly open or slam shut.
      • You alter the appearance of your eyes for 1 minute.
      Up to three of these effects can be active at a time.
    
    Acolyte background (Cleric cantrip)
  

  
  
    
      Minor Illusion ⭐
      Illusion Cantrip · Wizard · Illusionist (always known)
    
    Always Prepared
    
      Casting TimeAction or Bonus Action
      Range90 ft (30+60 Illusionist)
      ComponentsS, M (fleece)
      Duration1 minute
    
    
      Improved Minor Illusion (Illusionist): Create a sound AND an image simultaneously with a single casting. Can be cast as a Bonus Action. No verbal component needed.
      Sound: Any sound you choose originating from any point within range — from a whisper to a scream.
      Image: An object no larger than a 5-foot cube. No sound, smell, texture, or temperature. A creature that physically interacts with it can make an Investigation check vs. DC 15 to disbelieve.
    
    Wizard spellbook · Illusionist subclass (always known) · No verbal needed
  

  
  
    
      Toll the Dead
      Necromancy Cantrip · Magic Initiate (Cleric)
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range60 ft
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      You point at one creature you can see within range, and the sound of a dolorous bell fills the air around it for a moment. The target must succeed on a WIS saving throw (DC 15) or take necrotic damage.
      The target takes 1d8 necrotic damage. If the target is missing any of its Hit Points, it instead takes 1d12 necrotic damage.
    
    Cantrip Upgrade: 2d8/2d12 at level 5 · 3d8/3d12 at level 11 · 4d8/4d12 at level 17
    Magic Initiate feat (Cleric)
  

  
  
    
      Starry Wisp
      Evocation Cantrip · Magic Initiate (Cleric)
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range60 ft
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      You launch a mote of light at one creature or object within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes 1d8 radiant damage, and until the end of your next turn, it emits dim light in a 10-foot radius and can't benefit from the Invisible condition.
    
    Cantrip Upgrade: 2d8 at level 5 · 3d8 at level 11 · 4d8 at level 17
    Magic Initiate feat (Cleric) · Attack: +7
  



Level 1 Spells



  
  
    
      Command
      Enchantment · 1st Level · Cleric (Acolyte)
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range60 ft
      ComponentsV
      Duration1 round
    
    
      You speak a one-word command to a creature you can see within range. The target must succeed on a WIS saving throw (DC 15) or follow the command on its next turn.
      The spell has no effect if the target is Undead, if it doesn't understand your language, or if your command is directly harmful to it.
      Example commands: Approach (move toward you), Drop (drops held items), Flee (move away from you), Grovel (falls prone and ends turn), Halt (doesn't move, no actions/reactions).
    
    Higher Slots: Target one additional creature for each slot level above 1st.
    Acolyte background (Cleric spell) · Uses 1st-level slot
  

  
  
    
      Magic Missile
      Evocation · 1st Level · Wizard
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range120 ft
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      You create three glowing darts of magical force. Each dart unerringly strikes a target of your choice — no attack roll. Each dart deals 1d4 + 1 force damage. You can split them between any number of targets.
      Each dart is a separate instance of damage, which matters for effects that trigger on being hit.
    
    Higher Slots: +1 dart per slot level above 1st (4 darts @ 2nd · 5 @ 3rd…)
    Wizard spellbook · Uses 1st-level slot
  

  
  
    
      Mage Armor
      Abjuration · 1st Level · Wizard
    
    Superseded by medium armor
    
      Casting TimeAction
      RangeTouch
      ComponentsV, S, M (leather)
      Duration8 hours
    
    
      You touch a willing creature who isn't wearing armor. A protective magical force surrounds it, making its base AC equal to 13 + DEX modifier until the spell ends. The spell ends if the target dons armor.
      ⚠ No longer useful — you wear medium armor (better AC) as a Ranger.
    
    Wizard spellbook · Still in spellbook but not prepared
  

  
  
    
      Grease
      Conjuration · 1st Level · Magic Initiate (Cleric)
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range60 ft
      ComponentsV, S, M (butter)
      Duration1 minute
    
    
      Slick grease covers the ground in a 10-foot square centred on a point within range. That area becomes difficult terrain for the duration.
      When the grease appears, each creature standing in its area must succeed on a DEX saving throw (DC 15) or have the Prone condition. A creature that enters the area or ends its turn there must also succeed or fall Prone.
    
    Magic Initiate feat (Cleric) · Uses 1st-level slot
  

  
  
    
      Unseen Servant
      Conjuration · 1st Level · Wizard · Ritual
    
    Ritual
    
      Casting TimeAction / Ritual +10 min
      Range60 ft
      ComponentsV, S, M (string)
      Duration1 hour
    
    
      This spell creates an invisible, mindless, shapeless force that performs simple tasks at your command until the spell ends. It has STR 2, AC 10, and 1 Hit Point. It disappears if reduced to 0 HP.
      As a Bonus Action, you mentally command the servant to move up to 15 ft and interact with an object. It can open/close doors, carry up to 25 lbs, clean, pour drinks, hold torches, and similar tasks — but cannot attack.
    
    Wizard spellbook · Cast as ritual (no slot needed)
  

  
  
    
      Find Familiar
      Conjuration · 1st Level · Wizard · Ritual
    
    Ritual
    
      Casting Time1 hour (ritual)
      Range10 ft
      ComponentsV, S, M (10 gp consumed)
      DurationUntil dismissed
    
    
      You gain the service of a familiar, a spirit that takes an animal form of your choice: bat, cat, crab, frog, hawk, lizard, octopus, owl, rat, raven, sea horse, spider, or weasel.
      As an Action, you can see through the familiar's eyes and hear through its ears until the start of your next turn. You can communicate telepathically with it within 100 ft.
      When you cast a spell with a touch range, your familiar can deliver it as if it cast the spell, as long as it is within 100 ft of you.
      If the familiar drops to 0 HP, it disappears. You can resummon it by recasting the spell (consumes 10 gp again).
    
    Wizard spellbook · Cast as ritual (no slot needed)
  

  
  
    
      Comprehend Languages
      Divination · 1st Level · Wizard · Ritual
    
    Ritual
    
      Casting TimeAction / Ritual +10 min
      RangeSelf
      ComponentsV, S, M (soot, salt)
      Duration1 hour
    
    
      For the duration, you understand the literal meaning of any spoken language that you hear. You also understand any written language that you see, but you must be touching the surface on which the words are written. It takes about 1 minute to read one page of text.
      This spell doesn't decode secret messages or glyphs that aren't part of a written language.
      Does not grant the ability to speak or write the language.
    
    Wizard spellbook · Cast as ritual (no slot needed)
  

  
  
    
      Tenser's Floating Disk
      Conjuration · 1st Level · Wizard · Ritual
    
    Ritual
    
      Casting TimeAction / Ritual +10 min
      Range30 ft
      ComponentsV, S, M (mercury drop)
      Duration1 hour
    
    
      This spell creates a circular, horizontal plane of force, 3 feet in diameter and 1 inch thick, that floats 3 feet above the ground in an unoccupied space of your choice within range. The disk persists for the duration and can hold up to 500 pounds.
      If more weight is placed on it, the spell ends. The disk remains level even on inclined surfaces.
      If you move more than 20 feet away from it, the disk follows you. If you are ever more than 100 feet away from it, the spell ends.
    
    Wizard spellbook · Cast as ritual (no slot needed)
  

  
  
    
      Silent Image
      Illusion · 1st Level · Wizard (costs 2nd-level slot)
    
    C
    
      Casting TimeAction
      Range120 ft (60+60 Illusionist)
      ComponentsS, M (fleece) — no verbal (Illusionist)
      DurationConcentration, 10 min
    
    
      You create the image of an object, a creature, or some other visible phenomenon that is no larger than a 15-foot cube. The image appears at a spot within range and lasts for the duration. The image is purely visual — it has no sound, smell, or other sensory effects.
      As an Action, you can cause the image to move to any spot within range. As the image changes location, you can alter its appearance so that its movements appear natural for the image.
      Physical interaction reveals the image as an illusion. A creature that uses its action to examine the image can determine it is illusory with a successful Investigation check (DC 15).
    
    Wizard spellbook · Slot: 2nd level (Tiberius preference)
  

  
  
    
      Silvery Barbs
      Enchantment · 1st Level · Wizard (costs 2nd-level slot)
    
    Reaction
    
      Casting TimeReaction*
      Range60 ft
      ComponentsV
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      *Trigger: a creature within 60 ft succeeds on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw.
      You unleash a barrage of needle-like shards of silver that force the triggering creature to reroll the d20 and use the lower roll, potentially turning the success into a failure.
      You can also choose a different creature you can see within range (not the triggering creature). That creature gains advantage on the next attack roll, ability check, or saving throw it makes within 1 minute. A creature can have this benefit only once per casting.
      One of the strongest reaction spells in the game — can deny a critical hit or a passed saving throw.
    
    Wizard spellbook · Slot: 2nd level (Tiberius preference)
  

  
  
    
      Color Spray ⭐
      Illusion · 1st Level · Wizard · Prepared
    
    Prepared
    
      Casting TimeAction
      RangeSelf (15-ft cone)
      ComponentsS, M (sand/powder) — no verbal (Illusionist)
      Duration1 round
    
    
      A dazzling array of flashing, coloured light springs from your hand. Roll 6d10; the total is how many Hit Points of creatures this spell can affect. Starting with the creature that has the lowest current HP, each creature affected by this spell is Blinded until the end of your next turn.
      Creatures in the area are affected in ascending order of their current Hit Points. Subtract each creature's Hit Points from the total before moving to the next. A creature's HP must be equal to or less than the remaining total for the creature to be affected.
      Note: Can be cast at 1st or 2nd slot too — just affects fewer HP worth of creatures (no 3rd slot yet).
    
    Higher Slots: Roll an additional 2d10 for each slot level above 1st.
    Wizard spellbook · Can use any slot level (planned for 3rd when available)
  



Level 2 Spells



  
  
    
      Magic Weapon
      Transmutation · 2nd Level · Wizard
    
    C
    
      Casting TimeBonus Action
      RangeTouch
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationConcentration, 1 hour
    
    
      You touch a nonmagical weapon. Until the spell ends, that weapon becomes a magic weapon with a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls.
      This means it bypasses resistance and immunity to damage from nonmagical attacks — crucial against constructs, undead, and similar creatures.
      Great on your Warhammer or Light Crossbow before a fight you know involves resistant creatures.
    
    Higher Slots: +2 bonus with a 4th-level slot · +3 bonus with a 6th-level slot
    Wizard spellbook · Uses 2nd-level slot
  

  
  
    
      Nystul's Magic Aura
      Illusion · 2nd Level · Wizard (Illusionist)
    
    
    
      Casting TimeAction
      RangeTouch
      ComponentsS, M (silk square) — no verbal (Illusionist)
      Duration24 hours
    
    
      You place an illusion on a creature or object you touch so that divination spells reveal false information about it. The target can be a willing creature or an object not carried or worn by another creature.
      Choose one or both of the following effects when you cast the spell:
      False Aura: You change the way the target appears to spells and magical effects that detect magical auras, such as Detect Magic. You can make a nonmagical object appear magical, a magical object appear nonmagical, or change the object's magical aura to appear as a different school of magic you choose.
      Mask: You change the way the target appears to spells and magical effects that detect creature types, such as a paladin's Divine Sense. You choose a creature type and other spells treat the target as if it were that type.
      If you cast this spell on the same creature or object every day for 30 days, placing the same effect on it each time, the illusion lasts until it is dispelled.
    
    Wizard spellbook (Illusionist) · Uses 2nd-level slot
  

  
  
    
      Invisibility ⭐
      Illusion · 2nd Level · Wizard (Illusionist)
    
    CPrepared
    
      Casting TimeAction
      RangeTouch
      ComponentsS, M (eyelash in gum arabic) — no verbal (Illusionist)
      DurationConcentration, 1 hour
    
    
      A creature you touch becomes Invisible until the spell ends. Anything the target is wearing or carrying is Invisible as long as it is on the target's person.
      The spell ends for a target that makes an attack roll, deals damage, or casts a spell.
      No verbal component needed — Illusionist feature. Useful for silent scenarios.
    
    Higher Slots: You can target one additional creature for each slot level above 2nd.
    Wizard spellbook (Illusionist) · Uses 2nd-level slot
  




Ranger Spells



  
  
    
      Hunter's Mark ⭐
      Divination · 1st Level · Ranger · Always Prepared
    
    CAlways Prepared
    
      Casting TimeBonus Action
      Range90 ft
      ComponentsV
      DurationConcentration, 1 hour
    
    
      You choose a creature you can see within range and mystically mark it as your quarry. Until the spell ends, you deal an extra 1d6 damage to the target whenever you hit it with an attack roll. Also, if the target dies before this spell ends, you can use a Bonus Action to mark a new creature.
      ⭐ Favored Enemy (Hobgoblin): Hunter's Mark is always prepared and you can cast it twice per day without expending a spell slot. Both uses are regained on a Long Rest.
    
    Higher Slots: 3rd-level slot → Concentration up to 8 hours · 5th-level slot → Concentration up to 24 hours
    Ranger spell · WIS DC 11 · Favored Enemy: 2× free/day
  

  
  
    
      Cure Wounds ⭐
      Abjuration · 1st Level · Ranger · Prepared
    
    Prepared
    
      Casting TimeAction
      RangeTouch
      ComponentsV, S
      DurationInstantaneous
    
    
      A creature you touch regains a number of Hit Points equal to 2d8 + your WIS modifier.
      This spell has no effect on Undead or Constructs.
    
    Higher Slots: +2d8 for each slot level above 1st (4d8+WIS @ 2nd · 6d8+WIS @ 3rd…)
    Ranger spell · WIS modifier added to healing · Uses 1st-level slot

title: Illusion Tactics
text: Illusionist perks active on all tactics below: No verbal components for illusion spells · Minor Illusion casts as Bonus Action, creates sound + image simultaneously, range 90 ft · Silent Image range 120 ft

title: Illusion Tactics
text:
Minor Illusion
Cantrip · Bonus Action or Action · 90 ft · No concentration · No verbal · Creates BOTH sound AND image
The bonus action cast is your action economy engine — every round ask: “What does my Minor Illusion do here?”


  
    
      Phantom Reinforcements
      Combat
    
    
      How: Bonus Action — create an image of a soldier rounding a corner, plus the sound of armoured footsteps and a shouted command ("The Captain says fall back!"). Enemies must spend an Action to disbelieve it.
      Why it works: Forces hesitation or repositioning before enemies can use their Action. Free bonus action illusion that costs the enemy a full Action to resolve.
    
    Action economyDistraction
  

  
    
      Arrow Slit Wall
      Combat
    
    
      How: Bonus Action — place an illusory stone wall with arrow slits in front of your party. Enemies route around it. Allies fire through the slits. No concentration means your Action is free for a real spell.
      Why it works: Costs zero spell slots. Forces enemies to waste movement. Runs indefinitely while you cast other things.
    
    No slotsCoverMovement control
  

  
    
      Dead Guard Post
      Stealth / Social
    
    
      How: After a fight, project the slain guard still standing at their post with normal ambient sounds (shuffling, a cough). Passers-by see nothing wrong.
      Why it works: No concentration = runs indefinitely while you do other things. Buys the whole party time to search, interrogate, or loot without raising an alarm.
    
    No concentrationInfiltration
  

  
    
      Sound Bait
      Stealth
    
    
      How: At 90 ft range — completely out of visual contact — create a sound: a crash, coin jingle, distant scream, a door slamming. Pull enemies away from your position.
      Why it works: 90 ft range means you can redirect patrols from well out of danger. Creatures moving toward the bait are moving away from the party.
    
    90 ft rangePatrol redirect
  

  
    
      Panic Exit
      Social / Crowd
    
    
      How: Create an image of fire, flooding water, or structural collapse — with corresponding sound. Humanoids with survival instincts route toward exits.
      Why it works: No save required. You're creating environmental conditions that rational creatures respond to predictably. Especially potent in urban or social settings.
    
    No saveCrowd control
  

  
    
      Silent Decoy Self
      Stealth
    
    
      How: During stealth, Bonus Action — create an image of yourself around a corner with footsteps. Guards investigate the decoy; the party slips past.
      Why it works: No verbal component and Bonus Action means no Stealth check penalty and no interrupting concentration on other spells.
    
    No verbalBonus ActionStealth
  

  
    
      Ambush Anchor
      Combat
    
    
      How: Surprise round — Bonus Action Minor Illusion creates a boulder or cart between party and enemies. Melee allies have immediate hard cover. Use your Action for a real spell.
      Why it works: Cover + Action spell in the same round on zero spell slots. Strong opening round that costs nothing.
    
    Surprise roundCoverNo slots
  

  
    
      Bluff Object
      Social
    
    
      How: Conjure a visual of a sealed letter with a wax crest, a bag of gold, a key — to make a bluff credible. Looks real until physically touched.
      Why it works: You only need a few seconds of credibility. "I have the documents right here" buys time without Deception rolls against visual inspection.
    
    Deception aidSocial

title: Illusion Tactics
text:
Silent Image
1st Level (2nd-level slot) · Action · 120 ft · Concentration 10 min · No verbal · 15-ft cube, movable
Silent Image is your battlefield architect spell. The 15-foot cube is enormous — think entire rooms, not just objects.


  
    
      Illusory Wall + Arrow Slits
      Combat
    
    
      How: Place a stone wall across a corridor. Add arrow slits. Enemies route around it. Allies fire through the slits. Move it with your Action if needed.
      Why it works: Full movement control for 10 minutes of concentration. At 120 ft range you're well behind the wall when you cast it.
    
    Movement control120 ft range10 min
  

  
    
      Decoy Monster
      Combat
    
    
      How: Create an image of a troll, giant spider, or a second Fighter. Move it toward enemies with your Action. They must spend their Action to disbelieve.
      Why it works: One enemy spends a full Action per round on nothing. Against a group, the decoy absorbs attention from multiple targets simultaneously.
    
    Action taxThreat redirect
  

  
    
      False Egress Trap
      Combat
    
    
      How: Create an image of a doorway or open corridor on a solid wall. Enemies in pursuit charge toward it, hit the real wall, and disbelieve — after wasting movement and potentially taking opportunity attacks.
      Why it works: Works best combined with real difficult terrain or allies waiting at the actual exit.
    
    Pursuit trapOA setup
  

  
    
      Dead Zone Floor
      Combat
    
    
      How: Create an image of a pit, lava, or flooded floor across a chokepoint. Enemies go around (wasting movement) or spend an Action to disbelieve.
      Why it works: Most humanoids don't voluntarily step into lava. This is concentration-based crowd control for a 2nd-level slot.
    
    Crowd controlChokepoint
  

  
    
      Status Quo Guard
      Stealth / Heist
    
    
      How: After defeating guards, create an image of them continuing their patrol. Move the image with your Action each round. Outside NPCs see nothing unusual.
      Why it works: Buys the party as many rounds as you can maintain concentration to complete a heist objective. Move the "guard" naturally to keep it believable.
    
    HeistSustained deception
  

  
    
      Advantage Opening
      Combat Setup
    
    
      How: Before initiative, place Silent Image of a large obstacle between party and enemies. Ranged allies are now unseen attackers — advantage on the first attack roll of the fight.
      Why it works: Once the shot passes through the illusion it's revealed, but you've already banked the advantage. Stack with a Surprise round for maximum effect.
    
    AdvantagePre-combat

title: Illusion Tactics
text:
Color Spray
1st Level · Action · Self (15-ft cone) · No verbal · Blinded until end of your next turn
Blinded = advantage for all your allies on attacks against those targets + disadvantage on their attacks. It’s a one-turn team buff as much as a debuff.


  
    
      Advantage Package
      Combat
    
    
      How: Lead with Color Spray before your party's heaviest hitter attacks a high-AC target. Every ally attacking a Blinded creature has advantage.
      Why it works: Against a boss, this is ~+4–5 expected damage per ally before accounting for crit probability. Blinded also blocks reactions requiring sight.
    
    Advantage for partyBoss fight
  

  
    
      Caster Shutdown
      Combat
    
    
      How: Target the enemy caster. A Blinded spellcaster cannot see targets, so spells requiring "a creature you can see" (Fireball, Hold Person, etc.) cannot be used against your party for one turn.
      Why it works: 1st-level slot interrupts a high-level enemy action. Enemy casters often have middling CON — the save is beatable.
    
    Spell denialPriority target
  

  
    
      Escape Cone
      Retreat
    
    
      How: When fleeing, Color Spray the cluster nearest you. Blinded enemies cannot see where you run and cannot make opportunity attacks against targets they can't see (2024 rules).
      Why it works: One slot lets the entire party disengage and flee safely if pursuing enemies are in the cone.
    
    RetreatOA prevention
  

  
    
      Crowd Scatter
      Social
    
    
      How: In a riot or mob situation, Color Spray into the crowd. Blinded commoners don't fight — they flee. No lethality.
      Why it works: Crowd control with zero kills, which matters if the party needs a clean political record. Scatter a blocking mob instantly.
    
    Non-lethalCrowd control
  

  
    
      Spray-and-Illusion Combo
      Combo
    
    
      How: Action — Color Spray. Bonus Action — Minor Illusion blocking the blinded enemies' escape route. They can't see which way to run, and your illusion psychologically blocks the exit.
      Why it works: Fully self-sufficient opening round using both Action and Bonus Action. No party coordination needed.
    
    Self-comboBonus ActionOpening round
  

  
    
      Ambush Opener
      Combat
    
    
      How: In a prepared ambush, Color Spray the moment enemies enter your kill zone — before any of them react. Allies knew the plan; they immediately attack with advantage.
      Why it works: Enemies act last, Blinded, with disadvantage on everything. Front-loads the combat disproportionately.
    
    AmbushFront-load

title: Illusion Tactics
text:
Invisibility
2nd Level · Action · Touch · Concentration 1 hour · No verbal · +1 target per slot above 2nd
In 2024: attacks against you have Disadvantage, your attacks have Advantage, you are unseen. Ends if you attack, deal damage, or cast a spell. Encourages non-combat use.


  
    
      Forward Scout
      Stealth
    
    
      How: Cast Invisibility on yourself, move ahead to observe enemy positions, count guards, identify casters, note traps, then return. Up to 1 hour, no attacks needed.
      Why it works: Party enters with a full tactical picture. No Perception check can see you if they rely on sight.
    
    Scouting1 hour
  

  
    
      Upcast Party Escort
      Stealth
    
    
      How: At 3rd-level slot — Invisibility on two creatures. At 4th level — three. Cast on the whole party before a critical stealth passage.
      Why it works: Guards auto-fail Perception checks relying on sight against Invisible creatures. Near-guaranteed stealth pass for one dangerous zone.
    
    UpcastParty stealth
  

  
    
      Reposition Without OA
      Combat
    
    
      How: Cast Invisibility on yourself, reposition freely in combat. Opportunity attacks require seeing the target (2024 rules) — you move with impunity.
      Why it works: Repositioning in combat normally costs Disengage or provokes OAs. Invisibility removes this constraint for as long as you don't attack.
    
    RepositioningOA immunity
  

  
    
      Potion Under Cover
      Survival
    
    
      How: When bloodied, cast Invisibility and break from combat. Use your next turn to drink a healing potion — drinking doesn't break Invisibility (no attack, no damage, no spell).
      Why it works: Enemies can't target you, can't OA you, and can't see which direction you fled. Buys a full turn of safe healing.
    
    SurvivalHealing
  

  
    
      Rescue Drag
      Rescue
    
    
      How: 3rd-level slot — cast on yourself AND an unconscious or downed ally. Drag the ally to safety. No OAs on either of you while you move.
      Why it works: One slot buys a safe extraction of a dying party member who would otherwise be executed on their turn.
    
    Rescue3rd-level slot
  

  
    
      Diplomatic Eavesdrop
      Social / Intel
    
    
      How: In a social setting (court, negotiation, tavern meeting), Invisibility lets you move around eavesdropping, examining documents, or passing objects without detection.
      Why it works: You can whisper to allies who can hear you. Excellent for gathering intelligence during events the party is attending openly.
    
    IntelligenceSocial

title: Illusion Tactics
text:
Nystul’s Magic Aura
2nd Level · Action · Touch · 24 hours (permanent after 30 consecutive days) · No verbal · Hides or fakes magical aura / creature type
This is an information warfare spell. It attacks the intelligence systems enemies use to identify threats. Best used in planning, not reaction.


  
    
      Gear Smuggling
      Social / Infiltration
    
    
      How: Cast on any magic item to make it appear nonmagical to Detect Magic. Cross checkpoints and guard inspections without losing your gear. Recast every 24 hours.
      Why it works: Completely reliable. Spellbook, Javelin of Lightning, magical armour — all appears mundane to any inspection short of True Seeing.
    
    InfiltrationGear protection
  

  
    
      False School
      Social
    
    
      How: Change a magic item's apparent school. A politically toxic Necromancy item appears as Transmutation. Show gear to factions without revealing its true nature.
      Why it works: Factions that react differently to different schools can be manipulated. Show the church your "Transmutation staff" that's actually Necromancy.
    
    Faction politicsDeception
  

  
    
      Creature Type Mask
      Utility
    
    
      How: Cast on a party member or NPC to change their apparent creature type for all spells and magical effects. Make an Undead companion appear as a Humanoid — it can be healed and won't trigger Turn Undead.
      Why it works: Also protects allies from creature-type-specific spells (Charm Person, Hold Person only work on Humanoids). Mask your Fighter as a Construct to make them immune to those spells from hostile casters.
    
    Spell immunityUndead allies
  

  
    
      False Threat Plant
      Deception
    
    
      How: Cast on a mundane object to make it appear magical (with any school you choose). Plant it somewhere enemies will detect it. They waste time investigating and neutralising a fake magical threat.
      Why it works: Draws enemy casters into preparing countermeasures against something that doesn't exist. Classic misdirection.
    
    MisdirectionEnemy action waste
  

  
    
      The Long Con (30 Days)
      Campaign
    
    
      How: With 30 consecutive days of casting on the same target, the effect becomes permanent. A cursed item appears clean forever. A forbidden artefact appears mundane. A wanted criminal appears as a different creature type to all magical detection permanently.
      Why it works: World-altering effect from a 2nd-level slot investment during downtime. Best long-term investment in the spellbook.
    
    PermanentDowntimeCampaign-level

title: Illusion Tactics
text:
Cross-Spell Combos


  
    
      Silent Stalker
      Combo
    
    
      Spells: Invisibility + Minor Illusion (Bonus Action)
      You're invisible. Drop an auditory distraction 90 ft away in a different direction. Guards investigate the sound while you slip past.
    
    InvisibilityMinor IllusionInfiltration
  

  
    
      Full Decoy
      Combo
    
    
      Spells: Silent Image + Minor Illusion (Bonus Action)
      Silent Image creates a moving figure; Minor Illusion adds its voice and footsteps. Stack both to create the most convincing possible fake person without spending a Major Image slot.
    
    Silent ImageMinor IllusionDeception
  

  
    
      Spray and Block
      Combo
    
    
      Spells: Color Spray (Action) + Minor Illusion blocking exit (Bonus Action)
      Blind the cluster, then immediately drop an illusion blocking the direction they'd flee. They can't see the exit, and your illusion psychologically blocks the gap.
    
    Color SprayMinor IllusionTrap
  

  
    
      Ghost Patrol
      Combo
    
    
      Spells: Silent Image (moving figure) + Minor Illusion (sound) + Nystul's Aura (pre-cast on the party)
      Fake guard patrols with convincing movement and sound while the party's own magical signatures are hidden. Total information blackout for any watching enemy.
    
    Silent ImageNystul'sHeist
  

  
    
      Wrapped Scout
      Combo
    
    
      Spells: Nystul's Magic Aura (pre-cast, hides gear) + Invisibility
      Nystul's masks your spellcasting signature. Invisibility makes you physically unseen. You pass every layer of magical and physical detection simultaneously.
    
    Nystul'sInvisibilityScouting
  








Physical interaction disbelieves an illusion. Enemies who walk through a wall, fire into apparent smoke, or touch a fake object get to make an Investigation check vs. DC 15 to see through it. Plan your illusions so the enemy has no reason to physically interact — that’s the real skill.
